description: Search forward from a start time for the next occurrences of one sky-event class, selected by the `event` enum: solar_eclipse, lunar_eclipse, equinox, solstice, moon_quarter, opposition, conjunction, max_elongation, or perigee_apogee. Both eclipse classes take an optional observer (latitude and longitude together). solar_eclipse without one returns global eclipses — kind, peak time, obscuration, and for a total or annular eclipse the latitude/longitude where it is greatest; with one it returns only eclipses visible from that point, with local contact times, `local_visible`, and the Sun's altitude at each contact. lunar_eclipse returns geocentric contact times, the same instants everywhere on Earth; an observer adds `local_visible` and the Moon's altitude at each contact. Every other class is geocentric and ignores a location. The body-relative events (opposition, conjunction, max_elongation, perigee_apogee) require a `body`: opposition applies to the superior planets (mars through pluto), conjunction to any planet, max_elongation to mercury and venus, and perigee_apogee to the moon (perigee/apogee), earth, or a planet (perihelion/aphelion). conjunction with `body` alone is that planet's conjunction with the Sun. Add `body2` for a conjunction of two bodies — the Moon or a planet with another: the instant they share one ecliptic longitude seen from Earth's center, with their `separation_degrees` at that instant. That separation is not always their closest approach, since two planets can pass closer days or weeks away, and listings that time conjunctions by right ascension differ by hours, or by days for slow pairs. Returns the next `count` occurrences (default 1), up to 20 per call: a larger `count`, up to 200, returns the first 20 and a notice naming the exact `start` and `count` that continue the series. Searches stop at the end of 2100, the close of the supported span; when that leaves fewer than `count`, a notice says so. Start defaults to now; pass an IANA `timezone` for observer-local timestamps.

body.description: Target body — required for opposition, conjunction, max_elongation, and perigee_apogee; ignored otherwise. "earth" is accepted only for perigee_apogee, which returns its perihelion and aphelion. With `body2`, the Moon or a planet.

body2.description: Second body for a conjunction of two bodies: the Moon or a planet, different from `body`. Accepted only with event "conjunction", where it replaces the conjunction of `body` with the Sun by the conjunction of `body` and `body2` in ecliptic longitude seen from Earth's center. For the Moon meeting the Sun, search moon_quarter for the new moon.

count.description: Number of forward occurrences to return. Default 1. At most 20 are computed per call; a count up to 200 returns the first 20 with a notice naming the `start` and `count` that continue the series.

elevation.description: Observer elevation in meters above sea level. Default 0.

event.description: Which class of event to search for.

latitude.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees, supplied together with longitude. Optional for solar_eclipse and lunar_eclipse, where it adds local circumstances; omit both for a global solar search. Ignored by every other event.

longitude.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, supplied together with latitude. Optional for solar_eclipse and lunar_eclipse; ignored by every other event.

start.description: Search start as an ISO 8601 UTC string, e.g. "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z". Defaults to now. A value with no zone designator is read as UTC, not the local zone of the server process.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for localized output, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles". When omitted, output is UTC-only.

name: astronomy_find_events

cap.description: The per-call event cap that was applied.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `incomplete_observer`: A solar_eclipse or lunar_eclipse was requested with only one of latitude and longitude. `body_required`: A body-relative event was requested without a target body. `body_not_supported`: The body has no such event — opposition for the Sun, Moon, Earth, or an inner planet; conjunction without `body2` for the Sun, Moon, or Earth; max_elongation for anything but mercury or venus; perigee_apogee for the Sun. `invalid_body_pair`: `body2` was supplied with an event other than conjunction, names the same body as `body`, or is paired with a `body` of sun or earth. `invalid_time`: The `start` value is not a parseable ISO 8601 instant, or names a calendar date that does not exist (e.g. 2026-02-30). `time_out_of_range`: The requested start instant is outside the engine's high-accuracy span (≈1900–2100). `invalid_timezone`: The `timezone` value is not an IANA zone this runtime knows. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

events.description: The next occurrences of the requested event class, in chronological order.

items.description: One event occurrence; which detail fields are present depends on the event class.

apsis_kind.description: Apsis classification. Present for perigee_apogee events.

body.description: The target body — the first of the pair for a two-body conjunction. Present for opposition/conjunction/max_elongation/perigee_apogee.

body2.description: The second body of a two-body conjunction, as requested. Present only when `body2` was supplied.

conjunction_kind.description: Whether the planet passes between Earth and the Sun (inferior) or behind the Sun (superior). Present only for mercury and venus conjunctions with the Sun, the two bodies that reach both.

contact_altitudes_degrees.description: Apparent altitude in degrees of the eclipsed body (the Sun for solar_eclipse, the Moon for lunar_eclipse) above the observer's horizon at each contact, keyed by bare phase name: partial_begin, total_begin, peak, total_end, partial_end, plus penumbral_begin and penumbral_end for a lunar eclipse. Negative means below the horizon; null marks a phase this eclipse does not reach. Present only when latitude/longitude are supplied.

contacts.description: Eclipse contact times in ISO 8601 UTC keyed by phase (e.g. partial_begin_utc, peak_utc); a phase that does not occur is null. A global solar eclipse carries peak_utc only.

distance_au.description: Center-to-center distance at the apsis in astronomical units. Present for perigee_apogee.

distance_km.description: Center-to-center distance at the apsis in kilometers. Present for perigee_apogee.

elongation_degrees.description: Greatest-elongation angle in degrees from the Sun. Present for max_elongation.

event.description: The event class this record belongs to.

kind.description: Eclipse classification: "penumbral", "partial", "annular", or "total". Present for eclipses.

local_visible.description: True when the eclipsed body — the Sun for solar_eclipse, the Moon for lunar_eclipse — is above the observer's horizon at any contact. Present only when latitude/longitude are supplied. A solar result with an observer is always true, because the local search returns only eclipses with the Sun up at first or last contact; contact_altitudes_degrees tells an eclipse at sunrise or sunset from one at midday.

obscuration.description: Peak fraction of the disc obscured, 0 to 1. Null/absent when undefined for a global partial solar eclipse.

peak_latitude_degrees.description: Geographic latitude in degrees where a total or annular solar eclipse is greatest. Present for a solar_eclipse searched without an observer; absent for a partial eclipse, whose shadow axis misses Earth.

peak_longitude_degrees.description: Geographic longitude in degrees where a total or annular solar eclipse is greatest. Present for a solar_eclipse searched without an observer; absent for a partial eclipse.

quarter.description: Which lunar quarter. Present for moon_quarter events.

separation_degrees.description: Angular separation in degrees between body and body2 seen from Earth's center at the conjunction instant. Not always their closest approach: two planets can pass closer days or weeks away. Present only for a two-body conjunction.

time_local.description: Event time in observer-local time, present only when a timezone was supplied.

time_utc.description: Time of the event (peak, for eclipses) in ISO 8601 UTC.

visibility.description: Whether the apparition is in the morning or evening sky. Present for max_elongation.

which.description: Which equinox or solstice. Present for equinox/solstice events.

notice.description: Why the list is shorter than the requested count: either the per-call cap held events back, and the notice names the exact `start` and `count` to re-call with, or the search reached the end of the supported span (2100). Absent when every requested occurrence came back.

shown.description: Number of events returned when the cap applied.

truncated.description: True when `count` exceeded the per-call cap and only the first events came back.

title: astronomy-mcp-server: find sky events
